title: The Russo-Ukrainian war: control, forces, outcomes and diplomacy
summary: Territory changes hands at a front reported as dated, located updates; forces are placed by open-source mapping; outcomes (ceasefire, peace, concessions, escalation) are priced by deadline in prediction markets; diplomacy is reported in the news.

concepts.label: Territorial control
concepts.description: Who holds an area, as DeepStateMap draws it.

children.label: Occupied since 2022
children.description: Held by Russia since the full-scale invasion.

children.label: Occupied since 2014
children.description: Crimea and the parts of Donetsk and Luhansk held since 2014.

children.label: Terrain
children.description: Elevation (m) from GMRT: rivers, ridges and plains shape where a front can move.

concepts.label: Front-line change
concepts.description: A place DeepStateMap reports changing hands, dated and located.

concepts.label: Force position
concepts.description: Where open-source mapping places military forces and infrastructure; a placement, not a confirmed location.

concepts.label: Outcome by deadline
concepts.description: A yes/no outcome with a date: does X happen by (or does Y last through) the deadline? Each prediction market prices one deadline; a series of them is the outcome's probability over time, a cumulative distribution for 'by' and a survival curve for 'through'.

facts.text: For 'X by d', P(by d1) <= P(by d2) whenever d1 < d2: a later deadline can only add ways to happen. A series that breaks this is mispriced or thin.
Market prices approximate probabilities only roughly: fees, the cost of locking up money until resolution, risk preferences and thin trading bias them, most at very low and very high prices.
A market resolves by its own written rules (what counts as a ceasefire, which source decides); read them before reading the price.

children.label: Market probability
children.description: The price of Yes (0 to 1), with the bid-ask spread and the money traded behind it.

children.label: Deadline
children.description: When the market resolves; its month and year are the 'before month-year X'.

children.label: Ceasefire
children.description: A mutually agreed halt to fighting (full or energy-only).

children.label: Peace deal
children.description: A signed agreement ending the war.

children.label: Territory
children.description: Ukraine ceding or recognising Russian control of territory.

children.label: Leadership
children.description: A change of head of state or an election.

children.label: Escalation
children.description: A clash with NATO, an attack on an EU or NATO country, mobilisation.

children.label: Alliances & guarantees
children.description: NATO membership or neutrality, security guarantees.

children.label: Play-money forecast
children.description: Manifold's markets: play money, more questions, fewer traders; a second opinion beside the priced ones.

concepts.label: Diplomatic development
concepts.description: Talks, meetings, ceasefire proposals, sanctions and UN action, as reported by UN News and indexed by GDELT.

children.label: UN News
children.description: The UN's own news service (regional feed).

children.label: GDELT
children.description: Machine-indexed world news coverage (English here); one request every 5 seconds per address.

concepts.label: DeepStateMap.Live
concepts.description: A Ukrainian volunteer open-source map of the war, updated daily; its history goes back to 2022.

facts.text: DeepStateMap's updates are short notes ('The enemy advanced near X') with each place linked to its map.
